newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas bounces across the curve, prompt busiest.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas bounces across the curve, prompt busiest.

text.p: U.K. spot natural gas prices ticked up on Friday, with traders and brokers saying that most periods had gone up by around 0.20 pence to 0.30 penny a therm.
Most interest was seen in the short term, with a glut of trades seen for the weekend and various days and combinations of days next week.
There is no unexpected demand increase, with Transco forecasting consumption on Saturday at 141 million cubic metres (mcm), or 33 percent of peak day demand, compared with 150 mcm on Friday.

Further out, prices were also stronger. The third quarter was little changed, but Q4 was traded at least twice, at 13.20 pence and 13.50 pence. Offers were heard coming from 13.55 pence a therm by the close. Q1 was also stronger, as was the year from October.
But while the 1997 gas year strengthened, the 1998 year from October was more stable, so the contango between the two narrowed.

The 1998 year traded at 13.40 pence, and one trader said that when the 1997 gas year moves, it is the contango between the years which tends to vary rather than the outright level of gas year 1998. There were rumours that a spread was done between the year from April 1998 and calendar 1998, although this was not confirmed.
"It's definitely firming," said a dealer, referring to the whole of the forward curve. "Across the board it's bounced slightly on the back of shortcovering, but not many bids are seen."
Another said that despite the bounce on Friday, he saw the market likely to remain on a downward trend.
The IPE gas contract was untraded yet again on Friday, the second consecutive day on which nothing was done. Only 70 lots traded in the whole week on the futures contract.
